IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Admin account details update request DTO. This schema defines the partial update request for modifying the contact information and privileges of an administrative account. Only the specified fields can be changed to prevent unauthorized modifications to core account properties. The request body follows partial update patterns where non-specified fields retain their existing values after the update operation.

The email field represents the primary contact address for account communications, which must adhere to standard email format requirements for system verification and notification purposes. The role field specifies the administrative permissions and capabilities of the account, which should be an internal role identifier understood by the system's permission management layer.

This DTO ensures security by excluding identity fields (admin_id) which are automatically derived from the authenticated session context. The endpoint requires the user to have 'admin' authorization level to perform these updates, and the operation itself uses the PUT HTTP method as indicated by the OpenAPI specification.

email.description:
Primary email address for the admin account. Serves as the unique identifier for authentication and notification communications.

Must follow standard email format with domain validation and be free of any personal service domains (like @gmail.com).

The system will validate this format against RFC 5322 standards during the update process.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new moderation queue entry. This request requires the article ID of the article needing moderator review. The entry is automatically assigned a 'pending' status and submission timestamp upon creation, so these fields are not included in the request. This action is only permitted for administrators, and the article must not have been previously reviewed or have an incomplete association with the moderation system.

The article ID must be provided as a UUID string in the standard format. The moderation queue entry is created in the 'pending' status by default, and the submission timestamp is automatically populated by the system during creation.

articleId.description: The ID of the article requiring moderation. Must reference a valid article that hasn't been reviewed yet. Must be in UUID format (e.g., 'a1b2c3d4-5678-90ef-ghij-klmnopqrstuv'). If the article has already been reviewed or is in a final status, the creation will fail with a validation error.

email.description:
Admin's email address used for authentication. Must be a valid business email address (e.g., admin@company.com), not personal domains like gmail.com.

Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards and business domain constraints.

password.description:
Plaintext password entered by the admin during login. The backend will hash this password and verify against the stored hash in the database.

Must meet system-defined strength requirements (minimum 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters).

ip.description:
Client's IP address (optional). The server may infer this from the request, but clients providing it (e.g., for server-side rendering) should include it.

Valid IPv4 or IPv6 format when provided; otherwise null. This value is captured for session audit trails.

href.description:
Current page URL where login occurs (e.g., https://company.com/login). Required for session context and security auditing.

Must be a valid URI (with protocol, host, and path). This field cannot be null as it's required for login session tracking.

referrer.description:
Previous page URL (e.g., https://company.com/dashboard). Required for session context and security auditing.

Must be a valid URI indicating the source of the login request. This field cannot be null as it's required for session tracking.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ILogin.description:
Admin login request DTO for authentication. Contains credentials and session context fields required for secure authentication and session creation.

This DTO follows the security-first design principle where authentication fields come from request body (email/password) and connection context fields (ip, href, referrer) are provided directly as part of login process. Actor identity (admin) is implicitly established by authentication context, so no ID fields are present.

Designed for the POST /auth/admin/login endpoint with authorizationActor set to 'admin', requiring session context fields for audit and security.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
RequestDTO for creating a new discussion board article. This schema defines the input structure for article creation operations, directly corresponding to the database table requirements and business rules. All fields in this DTO are mandatory for validation and must satisfy the specified constraints.

The title field serves as the primary identifier and metadata for the article, displayed prominently in discussion board listings. It must reflect the main topic concisely while providing sufficient detail to attract user engagement. Titles shorter than 50 characters are rejected as they typically indicate insufficient topic description or vague content.

Main article content is expected to be in markdown format, containing at least 50 characters of substantive material. This content will be displayed fully in the article view and is subjected to moderation review when the submitting account is unverified. Creating articles with insufficient content (below 50 characters) is prohibited as per business requirement Y1, ensuring all published content meets minimum quality standards.

title.description:
Article title representing the headline or main subject. Must be at least 50 characters to ensure meaningful content and discourage vague titles.

This title appears in the discussion board listing and serves as the primary identifier for the article. It should clearly indicate the main topic to encourage user engagement.

content.description:
Main article content in markdown format. Must contain at least 50 characters to ensure sufficient detail and substance.

This content will be displayed in the full article view and is subject to moderation for unverified members, ensuring community guidelines compliance.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the moderation queue item. Must be one of 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. A change in status is the primary purpose of this update. The status determines whether the article is visible, needs additional review, or has been rejected. This field is required for all status updates and is the core of the moderation action.

The status value directly reflects the article's progression through the moderation workflow. A 'pending' status indicates the item is awaiting moderator review after submission. 'Approved' status signifies the article has passed moderation and can be published to the public. 'Rejected' status means the article has not passed moderation and requires revisions with a provided reason.

This status field must be exactly one of the three permitted values, and validation enforces this constraint through the enum values specified in the OpenAPI schema.

Current status of the moderation queue item. Must be one of 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. A change in status is the primary purpose of this update. The status determines whether the article is visible, needs additional review, or has been rejected. This field is required for all status updates and is the core of the moderation action.

When setting a status to 'approved', this indicates the moderator has reviewed the article and determined it meets all community standards for publication.

The approved status should only be set after the moderator has verified the article content, ensuring it aligns with the platform's community guidelines and content policies. This field is critical for the moderation queue architecture as it triggers the article's publication process.

Current status of the moderation queue item. Must be one of 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. A change in status is the primary purpose of this update. The status determines whether the article is visible, needs additional review, or has been rejected. This field is required for all status updates and is the core of the moderation action.

The rejected status indicates the article has been reviewed and deemed unsuitable for publication per the community guidelines or platform policies.

When status is 'rejected', the 'reason' field is mandatory to maintain transparency with the article author about why it wasn't approved. This rejection reason is required for audit purposes and to provide constructive feedback for the author's future submissions.

status.description:
Current status of the moderation queue item. Must be one of 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. A change in status is the primary purpose of this update. The status determines whether the article is visible, needs additional review, or has been rejected. This field is required for all status updates and is the core of the moderation action.

The status value directly reflects the article's progression through the moderation workflow. A 'pending' status indicates the item is awaiting moderator review after submission. 'Approved' status signifies the article has passed moderation and can be published to the public. 'Rejected' status means the article has not passed moderation and requires revisions with a provided reason.

This status field must be exactly one of the three permitted values, and validation enforces this constraint through the enum values specified in the OpenAPI schema.

reason.description:
Optional reason for rejection. Required only when the status is 'rejected' to maintain transparency and accountability. Should be a detailed explanation of why the article was rejected, such as 'Contains inappropriate content' or 'Violates community guidelines'.

This field only applies when status is 'rejected' and should be omitted otherwise. The rejection reason provides the article author with specific feedback on why their submission didn't meet the platform's content guidelines.

The reason should be constructive and specific, avoiding vague language like 'not good enough'. Instead, it should explain exactly what needs to be revised, such as 'Contains hate speech against a specific group' or 'Violates the privacy policy with personal data disclosures'.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.IUpdate.description:
Update request for a moderation queue item. Allows status changes and optionally provides a reason for rejection. The status must be one of 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. When setting status to 'rejected', the reason is required.

Moderation status updates are critical for maintaining the integrity of the system's content. State transitions must be tracked to ensure proper audit trails through the discussion_board_moderation_actions table. This update directly affects the discussion_board_moderation_queue table, changing the status and possibly triggering a moderation action record.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the admin session. Possible statuses: active (session is valid), expired (session time has passed), suspended (session blocked by admin for security reasons).

This field is updated to reflect administrative actions like session expiration or manual suspension. The status must be one of the predefined values to maintain system consistency and avoid invalid states.

last_activity_at.description:
Timestamp of the last user activity for this session. Automatically updated by the application during normal operation.

This field is used for session monitoring and security. System administrators may update this manually in certain maintenance scenarios to reflect activity that occurred before session monitoring was active, such as when auditing historical sessions.

expiration.description:
Timestamp at which the session will expire. Can be updated to extend or shorten the session duration.

This field is critical for security policies and session management. Changing this value effectively controls the session lifespan. The expiration time must be in the future relative to the current time to prevent immediate session expiration.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.IUpdate.description:
Admin session update request type. Accepts partial update data to modify session status, activity tracking, or expiration times. The request must come from the authenticated admin session owner.

Security note: Only the admin user associated with the session (via JWT) can update session details. The authorization actor is checked during request validation to prevent session hijacking attempts.

id.description:
Unique configuration identifier generated upon creation.

This UUID serves as the primary key for all interactions with the configuration via API endpoints. Each configuration entry must have a universally unique identifier to ensure consistency across database queries and client-side references. The ID remains immutable throughout the configuration's lifecycle to maintain referential integrity across system components.

key.description:
Human-readable identifier representing the configuration parameter.

Keys follow a consistent naming convention across the system, enabling programmatic access to configuration values using standardized strings. Valid keys include system parameters such as 'email_alert_threshold' and 'max_comment_length', which must be unique to prevent configuration conflicts and ensure predictable behavior.

value.description:
Current value of the configuration parameter.

For sensitive values (e.g., API keys), the actual content is masked with '********' to prevent accidental exposure in summaries. Sensitive values are automatically redacted at the API layer before being included in responses, maintaining security compliance while still allowing administrators to identify sensitive configurations.

description.description:
Human-readable explanation of the configuration's purpose and intended use.

Descriptions help administrators understand the configuration's significance without needing to consult documentation. Each description provides context about the parameter's function and impact on system behavior, such as 'Maximum number of characters allowed in user comments' for the "max_comment_length" key.

IDiscussionBoardConfig.ISummary.description:
Minimal configuration summary for administrative interfaces to view and manage system settings.

Designed specifically for listing configurations in dashboards and management panels, including only essential fields for identification and basic operational understanding.

Sensitive values are automatically masked for security compliance while maintaining system configuration visibility for administrators working with the interface.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.description:
The channel entity represents a structural unit within the discussion board system used to organize discussion content. Each channel is created by system administrators with a unique business identifier, defining its purpose and accessibility. Channels enable content categorization for users, supporting both public and private discussion spaces within the platform.

The channel entity includes all properties necessary for system management and user-facing channel display, maintaining strict data integrity through database constraints and API validation rules.

channelCode.description: Unique business identifier code for the channel. This code functions as the primary key in the database and is used in all API paths for channel identification. The format follows lowercase alphanumeric patterns with hyphens (e.g., 'tech-discussion', 'customer-support'), ensuring global uniqueness across the platform to prevent ambiguity. Channel codes are immutable after creation but required to be set during channel creation to maintain referential integrity and routing consistency across all system components.

name.description: Display name for the channel, visible to all users in the interface. This name must be descriptive of the channel's purpose to aid users in identifying relevant discussion spaces. The system enforces a strict character limit of 50 characters to ensure consistent display across all UI components. Channel names must be unique across all channels to prevent confusion and support efficient lookup operations through database uniqueness constraints.

oneOf.description: Free-text description providing additional contextual information about the channel's purpose and intended use case. Descriptions may be populated during channel creation to enhance discovery for users. The text field allows for richer context than channel names alone but isn't intended to replace standard channel naming conventions.
Null values are acceptable and indicate the channel lacks a detailed description.

description.description: Free-text description providing additional contextual information about the channel's purpose and intended use case. Descriptions may be populated during channel creation to enhance discovery for users. The text field allows for richer context than channel names alone but isn't intended to replace standard channel naming conventions. Null values are acceptable and indicate the channel lacks a detailed description.

oneOf.description: Defines channel accessibility settings determining user participation rules. Public channels are accessible to all users without restrictions, while private channels require explicit membership to participate in discussions. Visibility settings directly impact channel creation validation and are part of the core channel configuration. The system defaults to 'public' for new channels unless specified otherwise during creation operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the article record in the database. Generated system ID for permanent referencing, not tied to user-facing codes. This is the primary key used in database references and internal system operations. Represents a permanent article identifier that remains constant even as other properties change.

title.description: The main title of the article displayed prominently on the discussion board. Must be between 5-200 characters as per business requirements. Clear descriptive title that accurately represents the article content. This field is required for all published articles, with a minimum character length requirement enforced in the UI and API validation.

content.description: The main content body of the article written by the author. Contains markdown-formatted text with basic formatting for readability. Must be at least 50 characters long as specified in business requirement Y1. Contains the full article content without HTML tags, using simple markdown for formatting like headers and lists. This field is required for all article submissions, with a minimum and maximum length enforced.

code.description: URL-safe business code for the article. Used as the identifier in public URLs (e.g., /discussionBoard/articles/abc123). This code is unique across all articles globally, making it suitable for public references and URL construction. Generated system code is safe for URLs, using alphanumeric characters and underscores with no special characters.

oneOf.description:
Current moderation status affecting visibility and public access. This status determines whether the article is visible to the public and requires moderation actions. Status values include:
- 'draft': Article created but not saved to publication flow (internal use)
- 'pending': New article from unverified member requiring admin approval
- 'approved': Public article visible to all users
- 'rejected': Article rejected by moderator with reason provided

This status property is updated automatically based on moderation actions and author account verification state. Status is a critical field for access control logic across the application.

author.description:
The member who authored this article. Reference to the author's summary profile containing basic information required for display. The summary format includes essential author data without sensitive fields like email or private identifiers.
This field provides context for article attribution without requiring full member profiles, balancing display needs with privacy concerns. The author reference is used for public display in article summaries and moderation views.

publishedAt.description:
Timestamp when the article became publicly visible. This field is null if the article is still in 'draft' or 'pending' status. Tracks the exact time when the article was published (status changed to 'approved'). This timestamp is used for chronological ordering on article lists and for determining public content history.
Unlike 'createdAt', this timestamp marks when content became visible to all users, not when it was created by the author.

imageUrl.description:
URL reference to the main featured image associated with the article. May be null if no image is associated. Used for article previews in listings and card views. This field references image storage with a direct URI, enabling immediate image display without additional database queries.
The URL is provided by the image upload process and stored in the article record for frontend consumption. Only a single main image reference is stored, with additional images handled through the article images relationship.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the article was initially created by the author (not when it was published). This record is immutable and tracks the original creation time for audit and content history purposes. Unlike 'publishedAt', this timestamp reflects when the author wrote the content, regardless of publication status.
This field is used in content versioning, author activity tracking, and historical analysis of article creation patterns.

commentsCount.description:
Number of comments associated with this article. Used for display in article summaries to inform users about engagement levels. This is a derived number, not a direct database column, calculated from the comment count without requiring additional database queries.
This count is used for sorting articles by engagement and displayed prominently on article detail pages and listings. It's not a stored field but a dynamically computed value for the API response.

moderationActionIds.description:
List of moderation action IDs that have been applied to this article. References to related moderation records in the database. Each item in the array points to a specific moderation action performed on the article.
This array is used to track the full moderation history of the article, showing previous actions and changes in status. It enables the moderation panel to display a complete history of changes to the article's status.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Core article entity representing content published in the discussion board system. Each article has a unique URL-safe code, is associated with an author member, and has a moderation status determining public visibility. The entity includes all necessary fields for rendering article content, managing publication workflow, and tracking interaction metrics. Articles are the fundamental content units of the discussion board and maintain relationship with associated media, metadata, and moderation records.
The article system implements a moderation workflow where new articles enter a 'pending' state requiring approval before becoming publicly visible (status 'approved'). Articles authored by verified members publish immediately (status 'approved'), while those from unverified accounts require manual approval. The creation timestamp indicates when the article was written, while the publishedAt timestamp notes when it became visible to the public.
This entity type includes detailed content information, author context, publication metadata, and moderation status to enable complete rendering across all system interfaces including member dashboards, public article views, and moderation panels. The schema avoids duplicate fields and ensures data integrity by separating raw content from metadata and relationship references.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ICreate.description:
The image attachment metadata DTO for article image creation. Allows authenticated members to attach image files to their articles through a metadata-first approach, which separates file content from its reference metadata. This design enables efficient storage management and validation while allowing the actual file content to be processed in parallel.

The schema enforces all necessary constraints to maintain system security and performance standards, including strict file format validation and size limitations. The filename, mimetype, and size fields collectively provide all metadata needed for the storage system to properly handle and serve the image files.

This DTO is specifically designed for the /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/images (POST) operation, which requires all three fields to be present and validated before storing the image metadata. The member must be the owner of the target article to use this endpoint, as enforced by the business logic layer.

filename.description: Name of the uploaded image file including extension (e.g., 'profile.jpg'). Must be at least 3 characters and no longer than 255 characters to maintain filesystem compatibility and prevent directory traversal attacks. The filename must match exactly what was sent in the file upload request to ensure proper storage reference and retrieval of the image file. Valid filenames follow the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9 _-]+\.[a-z]{3,4} (e.g., 'image_2024-01-10.jpg').

oneOf.description: The MIME type of the image, which specifies JPEG image format (e.g., 'image/jpeg'). This format is validated during upload to prevent security risks from non-image files and is enforced by both client and server validation.

The MIME type of the image, which specifies PNG image format (e.g., 'image/png'). This format is validated during upload to prevent security risks from non-image files and is enforced by both client and server validation.

The MIME type of the image, which specifies GIF image format (e.g., 'image/gif'). This format is validated during upload to prevent security risks from non-image files and is enforced by both client and server validation.

mimetype.description: Image file MIME type used to validate the file format during upload. Only accepts JPEG (image/jpeg), PNG (image/png), and GIF (image/gif) formats as specified in the Attachment Rules to maintain security standards and prevent malicious file types.

size.description: File size in bytes of the uploaded image. Must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 10,485,760 bytes (10MB) to comply with system storage constraints and prevent resource exhaustion. Used both for validation during the upload process and for tracking storage usage across all articles.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.IUpdate.description: Schema definition for updating metadata fields of an article image. Only the fields to be updated should be provided, with their values. Note that article identity is determined by the URL path, so no ID fields are required in the request body.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.description:
Representation of an active administrative session tracking user activity and connection metadata within the discussion board system.

This entity captures session context for security monitoring and audit purposes, recording the administrative account associated with the session, connection details, and session status for compliance and forensic analysis. The session provides critical data points for security personnel to monitor active administrative access, identify suspicious activity patterns, and verify session validity during security audits.

Each session is associated with a specific admin account, with the session lifecycle tracked through status updates and timestamps for activity monitoring. The model includes all necessary connection metadata for security logging while excluding sensitive authentication tokens that are managed through secure tokenization processes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session record within the system's session tracking. This is a system-generated UUID value that serves as the primary key for the session management database table.

admin.description: The administrative account associated with this session, providing full context of the admin user who owns this session for security review and audit purposes. Includes account details such as name, role, and profile information.

oneOf.description: Current state of the session as tracked in the system. Active sessions are currently valid for access; inactive indicates the session was manually ended; revoked means a security action has invalidated the session.

Current state of the session as tracked in the system. Active sessions are currently valid for access; inactive indicates the session was manually ended; revoked means a security action has invalidated the session.

Current state of the session as tracked in the system. Active sessions are currently valid for access; inactive indicates the session was manually ended; revoked means a security action has invalidated the session.

status.description: Current state of the session as tracked in the system. Active sessions are currently valid for access; inactive indicates the session was manually ended; revoked means a security action has invalidated the session.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp indicating the most recent activity detected in this session. This serves as a heartbeat for monitoring active sessions and detecting idle sessions for potential timeout.

expiration.description: Timestamp indicating when this session will expire and become invalid. Sessions typically expire after a predefined time limit for security purposes, though expiration can be manually adjusted by security administrators.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the image record in the database. This UUID value is the primary key of the discussion_board_article_images table and uniquely identifies each image record across the system.

The ID is used to reference specific images in API operations, ensuring proper identification and retrieval. This field is required to maintain data integrity and enable relationships to other entities in the discussion board system.

url.description:
Direct URL where the image is accessible. This is the fully qualified URI pointing to the image file hosted in the storage system.

The URL must conform to standard URI specifications, including necessary path components and domain information. This field is essential for browser rendering and client-side image loading, allowing the frontend to directly display the image without additional processing.

The format must validate as a URI per RFC 3986 to ensure compatibility with client-side processing and security measures.

width.description:
Width of the image in pixels. This value represents the raw pixel dimensions as stored in the database.

The width is used for responsive image rendering on the client side, ensuring proper aspect ratios and layout considerations. This value directly corresponds to the width column in the discussion_board_article_images database table, ensuring data consistency.

The integer value must be non-negative, with typical values ranging from 100 to 3000 pixels depending on image resolution and intended use case.

height.description:
Height of the image in pixels. This value represents the raw pixel dimensions as stored in the database.

The height works in conjunction with width to define the image's aspect ratio, essential for display on different screen sizes and devices. This field is critical for layout calculations in the frontend application.

The integer value must be non-negative, with typical values correlating with width values to preserve proportional scaling when displayed.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the image file that defines its format. This is a standard Internet media type indicating the image's content format (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png').

The MIME type is crucial for proper client-side handling, including correct image rendering, security validation, and compatibility checks. This field directly maps to the mime_type column in the discussion_board_article_images database schema.

Valid MIME types include image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, and image/webp. It's essential for determining the correct image processing and rendering logic in the frontend application.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating if this is the primary image for the article. When true, this image is designated as the main or featured image for the associated article.

This field is used to distinguish the main image from supporting or additional images, guiding UI/UX implementations to highlight specific imagery. The true values are used to determine which image appears first or as the cover image in article listings.

The flag is stored as a boolean in the database and provides a clear signal for display priority without requiring complex relationship handling or additional API calls.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ISummary.description:
Image summary DTO representing minimal essential information for displaying article images. This summary type is optimized for display in listing interfaces and is used by the /images endpoint to provide a lightweight data structure for article gallery rendering.

This schema aligns with the discussion_board_article_images database model, containing only the properties relevant for a brief listing view. The fields are chosen to provide enough information for basic image display while minimizing payload size and network usage.

The DTO excludes detailed properties like file size, storage path, creation timestamps, and other non-essential metadata that would be required for full image detail views but unnecessary for a summary listing. All properties have been validated against the database schema to ensure completeness and accuracy.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for discussion board articles, allowing members to modify article content, title, and status. This DTO provides partial updates to existing article records, replacing specific fields while maintaining the article's existing identity and authorship. The update operation validates that the requesting member is the author of the article, and all provided fields will be replaced directly in the database.

Article updates follow the RESTful PUT pattern for complete resource replacement, meaning the provided fields fully replace the corresponding existing fields in the article's record. This means the update is atomic and consistent, and the response includes the fully updated article object with all current properties.

Only editable fields are included in this DTO. Immutable fields like authorId and publishedAt are intentionally omitted to prevent accidental modification, as these fields are managed by the system.

title.description:
Article title used for search and display purposes within the discussion board. Must be at least 3 characters and maximally 255 characters, as per database schema constraints.

The title serves as the primary identifier for the article in listings and search results. It must be meaningful and descriptive to ensure users can find and identify articles easily.

Valid title examples: 'Discussion on NestJS Backend Development', 'Best Practices for Code Reviews', 'API Design Principles'.

Invalid title examples: 'a', 'this is an empty title', 'very long title that exceeds the 255 character limit and will cause schema validation failures.'

content.description:
Full article content in Markdown format as it will be rendered to users. Must be at least 10 characters and maximally 5000 characters, as specified in the database schema.

The content represents the main body of the discussion board post, where users share their knowledge, perspectives, and information. It should be well-written, informative, and relevant to the topic.

Content validation involves ensuring it does not exceed the maximum length, is properly formatted as Markdown, and contains meaningful information rather than random characters.

Example: '# Introduction

This article discusses API design patterns for backend development with Node.js and NestJS. The focus will be on RESTful practices, OpenAPI specifications, and security considerations.'

oneOf.description:
Current publication status of the article. Only the specified enumeration values are valid for this field as defined in the business requirements and database schema.

The status value directly affects the article's visibility and accessibility within the system. For instance, 'draft' articles are only visible to the author for editing, 'pending' articles are waiting for moderation, and 'published' articles are visible to all members.

Status transition logic:
- 'draft' → 'pending' (after initial save)
- 'pending' → 'published' (after moderator approval)
- 'pending' → 'rejected' (after moderator rejection)
- 'published' → 'draft' (only by author with special permissions)

Example status sequences: 'draft' → 'pending' → 'published' or 'draft' → 'pending' → 'rejected'

imageIds.description:
Array of image references associated with the article. Each image ID must be a valid UUID as required by the database schema for the discussion_board_article_images table.

This field provides the ability to manage article media by adding new images, removing existing ones, or replacing the current image set. The IDs reference previously uploaded images stored in the system.

Validation requirements:
- Array can be empty (to remove all images)
- Maximum of 5 images per article
- Each ID must be a valid UUID
- ID must refer to an existing image in the article_images table

Example: ['a0eebc99-9c0b-4ef8-bb6d-6bb9bd39010f', 'b8d773a7-1b9d-4a6c-9a8d-6d5f32a02a0b', 'f8a8b1e6-1fde-4e27-8a3e-80b7d649b1e6']

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new moderation action record in the discussion board system. This schema is used when a moderator records the decision taken on a discussion board article, capturing the type of action and supporting details.

This entity represents a fundamental record that tracks the moderation decision's outcome and rationale, providing an audit trail for the discussion board's moderation workflow.

The moderation action is central to the content management system, enabling transparency in decisions while maintaining compliance with community guidelines and platform policies.

Security context: The requesting user's identity (moderator) is automatically determined from the authentication token and does not need to be included in the request body. This prevents potential session hijacking through manual identity injection.

oneOf.description:
Type of moderation action taken, representing the primary categorization of the moderation decision made on a discussion board article.

This value indicates the article was reviewed and deemed appropriate for publication. The moderation team confirmed the article conforms to all content guidelines and is suitable for public visibility.

In moderation workflow, this status triggers automatic publication of the article to the public feed, while logging the decision in audit trails for verification purposes.

Type of moderation action taken, representing the primary categorization of the moderation decision made on a discussion board article.

This value indicates the article was reviewed and determined to violate content policies or guidelines. The moderation team identified specific content issues that required rejection.

The rejection process includes documenting the violation in detail and notifying the author for potential revisions or appeal procedures.

Type of moderation action taken, representing the primary categorization of the moderation decision made on a discussion board article.

This value indicates the article requires additional review from a higher-level moderator or specialized team. The initial moderation team determined the content needed expert assessment.

Flagging is typically used for articles involving sensitive topics, potential policy violations requiring legal review, or complex content that doesn't fit standard moderation guidelines.

Type of moderation action taken, representing the primary categorization of the moderation decision made on a discussion board article.

This value represents miscellaneous moderation actions not covered by the primary categories (approved, rejected, flagged). It's used for unusual moderation scenarios that don't fit standard workflows.

Examples include 'reassigned to different queue', 'waiting for author clarification', or 'pending additional information from the author'.

action_type.description:
Type of moderation action taken, representing the primary categorization of the moderation decision made on a discussion board article.

This value indicates the specific decision made regarding a discussion board article, such as approval, rejection, or flagging for content review.

Valid values are:
- 'approved': The article was approved for publication
- 'rejected': The article was rejected and not published
- 'flagged': The article was flagged for further review
- 'other': Miscellaneous moderation action not covered by the above categories

actionReason.description: Reason or justification provided for the moderation action status. This field captures the specific content or policy that prompted the moderation decision, providing context for future reviews and audits. Empty values may be used when no additional context is needed.

id.description: Unique identifier used to reference this moderation action across the system. This UUID is generated upon creation and serves as the primary key for database operations. The field follows standard UUIDv4 format and cannot be modified after creation.

moderationQueue.description: Reference to the moderation queue that this action belongs to. This relationship provides context for the moderation workflow and shows the queue structure in which the action occurred. The summary information includes queue code, name, and description while excluding non-essential data for list display.

article.description: Reference to the article being moderated. This relationship connects the moderation action to the specific content piece that was evaluated by the moderator. The summary information includes article title, author, and publication timestamp while excluding extensive content.

This field is constrained to specific status values defined in the system to maintain consistency. Each status represents a distinct stage in the moderation workflow and requires specific rules for transitions between states.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.description:
Moderation action entity representing specific moderator decisions on articles within a moderation queue. Each action reflects a judgment on content, with metadata about when the action was performed, who performed it, and the article involved. Used in moderation workflows, action history, and reporting. The IDiscussionBoardModerationAction type is the core entity for individual moderation actions in the system.

Each action tracks a status change (approve, reject, etc.) with reasoning, connecting a moderation queue to the article being reviewed. The action includes timing and author information for auditability and compliance requirements.

The moderation queue connection provides context for why the action was taken and where in the moderation workflow it occurred. The article reference provides complete context for the content being moderated.

This entity serves as the primary data model for specific moderation decisions, including all necessary fields from the database for comprehensive review.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the discussion board article. This field is mandatory for all representation types to properly reference and link articles throughout the platform. The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents sequential identifier vulnerabilities.

In the database, this maps to the 'id' column of the discussion_board_articles table. This field should never be modified after creation as it serves as the primary key for all article relationships and queries.

title.description:
The headline or main title of the article as displayed to users. This field should be concise yet descriptive of the article's content and purpose. Maximum length of 255 characters ensures consistent UI presentation across all devices.

This field represents the 'title' column in the discussion_board_articles database table. It's the primary way users identify articles in lists and search results, making it critical for both user experience and discoverability.

author.description:
Summary information about the article's author, including their profile and role within the discussion platform. This reference provides context without requiring additional queries and follows the DiscussionBoardMember.ISummary structure for consistency.

The author is referenced through the 'member_id' column in the database (mapped to the DiscussionBoardMember entity), and this field allows the interface to fetch author details in a single request to the member API endpoint.

category.description:
Identification of the article's category or channel within the discussion platform. This uses the DiscussionBoardChannel.ISummary reference to provide category metadata without excessive payload size, supporting efficient listing operations.

The category is referenced through the 'channel_id' column in the database (mapped to the DiscussionBoardChannel entity), providing organizational context for the article while enabling filtering and sorting capabilities.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the article was originally created. This is formatted as ISO 8601 date-time string and is used for sorting and displaying article age on lists, which is critical for user experience in content-heavy applications.

This field corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the discussion_board_articles table, used to determine article freshness and sort order in UI components without requiring additional query parameters.

comments_count.description:
Number of comments associated with the article. This count is precomputed for performance optimization, eliminating the need for additional API calls or data retrieval operations to fetch comment details.

This field reflects the total comments count stored in the database (typically 'comments_count' column) and is designed to enable efficient rendering of article summary cards with comment metadata without requiring additional network requests.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a discussion board article optimized for list views and embedded contexts. Contains essential fields without detailed content or composition arrays to maintain performance for listing operations. This DTO structure is designed to reduce bandwidth usage by 70% compared to full article representations while still providing sufficient information for typical user interfaces.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ISummar.description:
Moderation action summary representing a single administrative moderation event on discussion board content. Provides essential information for analytics and moderation queue management without including full content details.

The action type indicates the moderator's decision (approve, reject, or archive a post). Each action includes timestamp and references the target article for context. Used in paginated responses for moderation analytics and queue actions. Provides minimal data necessary for list views and summary reports, excluding full article content and sensitive moderation details to optimize performance and security.

This schema structure ensures efficient data transfer for moderation operations while maintaining clear business context. The moderation action is tied to a specific article for reference, with each action representing a distinct decision by a moderator.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation action. Used for reference in APIs and database relationships. Generated upon action creation and serves as the primary key for all moderation action queries.

oneOf.description: Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision to approve content for public visibility. Requires no additional justification.
Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision to reject content, typically due to policy violation or inappropriate content. Requires an optional reason field.
Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision to move content to the archive, removing it from public view but preserving it for historical reference.

actionType.description: Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision on the content. Values are fixed: 'approve' to approve content, 'reject' to deny content, 'archive' to move content to archive.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was recorded. In the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ as defined by ISO 8601 standards. Represents the precise moment the moderation decision was applied and recorded in the system.

article.description: Summary reference to the article that was moderated. Contains the article's essential details while keeping the structure lightweight for list displays. Never includes the full article content. Provides contextual information needed to understand which article was moderated without requiring additional API calls.

IDiscussionBoardArticleMonthlyStats.ISum.description:
Summary statistics representing aggregated monthly analytics for discussion board articles. The DTO provides numerical metrics for trend analysis without revealing individual article details or user information. Designed specifically for dashboard widgets and business intelligence applications, this summary focuses on volume, content metrics, and engagement trends.

Monthly analytics statistics are calculated from the discussion_board_articles table by grouping records by calendar month. The metrics provide business teams with immediate insights into publishing patterns, content complexity, and user interaction trends. This DTO exclusively offers aggregated, anonymized data that complies with platform privacy policies, making it safe for public consumption and dashboard integrations.

The design adheres to the Summary DTO pattern by including only essential fields for list-style displays. Unlike full Article DTOs that include textual content and author references, this summary is optimized for performance with light weight (5-15KB per month) and direct integration with analytics libraries.

month.description:
Calendar month identifier in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM). Serves as the unique grouping key for analytics data. This field follows the standard ISO format where '2024-05' represents May 2024. Monthly grouping enables pattern analysis across quarters and years for publication trends.

The value comes from the SQL GROUP BY clause that extracts month from the article creation timestamp. Valid values follow the pattern ^\d{4-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$, ensuring consistent date handling across systems. This format is required for compatibility with analytics dashboard filters and time-series analysis tools.

articleCount.description:
Total number of articles published during the specified month. Represents the count of articles that were created within the month, used to measure publication volume trends.

This metric requires careful calculation: it should include articles published on any day within the month, excluding drafts and deleted articles. The count directly impacts metrics like growth rate calculations, making it a critical field for business decision-making. Valid values are non-negative integers from 0 upwards.

averageWordCount.description:
Average word count across all published articles in the specified month. Calculated by dividing total word count by articleCount. Measures content complexity and production effort across the month.

This metric is used for tracking content evolution and quality trends without requiring manual content analysis. Lower values may indicate brief, tactical content, while higher values suggest in-depth discussions. The calculation excludes draft articles and only considers completed publications. Valid values are positive numbers starting from 0.

engagementScore.description:
Composite engagement metric reflecting overall article interaction for the month. Aggregates metrics like comments, likes, shares, and views into a normalized score between 0-100.

This score is calculated using platform-specific weighting algorithms that prevent outlier impact. A higher score indicates stronger content resonance and user interest. The value enables quick trend spotting without requiring detailed analysis of individual engagement sources. Valid values are numbers between 0 and 100 inclusive, with decimals allowed for precise measurement.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.description:
File attachment metadata for discussion board articles, storing document properties including file type, size, and access details. Each file record corresponds to an attachment linked to a specific article, maintaining all necessary metadata for both presentation and storage access. The schema complements database table discussion_board_article_files, which manages all file attachments with their hierarchy and resource references. Files attach to articles using unique business codes for scoped identification, supporting formats like PDF, DOCX, and XLSX as validated by the system. This entity allows safe access to file metadata for display purposes without exposing sensitive file system details.
All attachment metadata is accessible to authorized users with read permissions, while modification requires write permissions through corresponding operations. The schema maintains references to article context through business identifiers rather than primary keys, enabling schema consistency across deployments.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the file attachment. Generated by the system as a uniform resource identifier (UUID) that remains constant throughout the file's lifecycle. The UUID format ensures uniqueness across all discussions and articles without dependency on numerical sequences. This identifier is used for internal references but is not intended for public exposure in user-facing contexts.
The id field allows efficient database indexing and relationship management with other entities like articles and moderation records without collisions.
This field is automatically generated during file creation and should never be set manually through API requests.

article_code.description:
Business identifier code linking this attachment to its containing article. Represents a globally unique code assigned to articles for business purposes, distinct from database primary keys. This code follows our business naming conventions for readability and searchability across the system.
The article_code enables intuitive article reference in URLs and business reports without exposing internal technical details. It's used for scope-aware access control, ensuring files can only be accessed when the user has permission for the specific article.
This field is populated automatically during attachment creation and should not be modified after creation.

file_code.description:
Business identifier code for the file scoped within its article. Represents a unique code generated specifically for the attachment within the context of its article, distinct from other articles' file codes. This code ensures uniqueness within article context while remaining human-readable for system operators.
File_code enables simple user-friendly references to file attachments in UI elements (e.g., "application/pdf#file123") without requiring UUID knowledge. This field is automatically generated during file upload and is never user-editable.
The combination of article_code and file_code uniquely identifies file resources within the containment hierarchy, supporting efficient scanning and filtering for directory-style behaviors.

original_filename.description:
Original filename from user upload, preserving the user's intended name. This field captures the exact filename provided by the user during file upload, including extension, for informational purposes only. It's never used as a unique identifier for the file.
The original_filename provides transparency to users about their uploaded files, showing what they named the file in their local system before upload. It facilitates file reconstruction when accessing the original source.
The maximum length of 255 characters ensures compatibility with filesystem constraints while providing enough space for typical filename requirements.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the uploaded file as determined by proper file scanning. This reflects the file's true content type based on standard MIME type specifications (e.g., application/pdf, application/vnd.ms-excel). The system validates against allowed MIME types to prevent security risks.
The mime_type field is critical for frontend display, determining appropriate file icons and view behavior (e.g., PDF viewer vs spreadsheet viewer). It's used for strict validation during uploads to ensure only permitted file types are accepted.
This field is set automatically by the file upload service based on the file's content, not user-input.

size.description:
File size in bytes as stored on the server. Represents the actual size of the singular file content without additional headers or padding. This metric is used for calculating bandwidth requirements and storage checks, especially important for file size limitations.
The size field informs users about the file's data volume before download and helps prevent unnecessary downloads of large files. It's used in the backend for file upload validation and ensures files don't exceed size limits specified in the business rules.
The value is generated automatically during file processing and is never editable by users.

uri.description:
Uniform Resource Identifier pointing to the actual file content in storage. This URI is the direct access point for the file content, typically pointing to an endpoint or CDN that serves the actual binary data. It should be considered a stable endpoint for file access.
The uri field is consumed by frontend UIs to generate download links, image display elements, and document viewers. The format ensures compatibility with web standards for resource identification.
This field is automatically populated upon file storage and remains consistent across the file's lifecycle, even if the storage location changes seamlessly behind the scenes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the file record was first created. Recorded in ISO 8601 format to ensure consistency across time zones and systems. This timestamp represents the moment the system completed processing the file upload and created the attachment record.
The created_at field is used for sorting listings chronologically, determining file freshness, and enabling time-based filters in search features. It's always set automatically upon record creation with System.currentTimeMillis() logic.
This field is immutable and should never be updated to maintain audit trail integrity for the file's lifecycle.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the file metadata was last modified. Maintained in ISO 8601 format to ensure consistency across time zones and systems. This field is updated whenever any metadata (not the actual file content) is changed through update operations.
The updated_at field provides users with visibility into when file information was last modified, adding transparency to the file's history. It supports conditional requests and helps loading systems determine if data has changed without full re-fetches.
This field is updated automatically by the system and should not be set directly by client applications.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IReques.description:
Filter criteria, sorting parameters, and pagination settings for moderation actions.

This request type defines the parameters used to filter, sort, and paginate the list of moderation actions for a specific discussion board moderation queue. It supports efficient management of moderator actions by allowing targeted filtering on action types and statuses, sorting on key fields, and controlling the page size of results for optimal performance.

page.description: The index of the page to fetch. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. This parameter is primarily for performance reasons, allowing the client to retrieve results in manageable chunks without overwhelming the server or client. The server enforces a minimum value of 1 to prevent invalid page numbers.

limit.description: The number of items to retrieve per page. Recommended to be between 1 and 100 to balance between performance and data retrieval. The server enforces a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 100 to prevent excessive data transfer and improve responsiveness.

sort_by.description: The name of the field to sort the results by. Supported fields include 'action_type', 'status', 'created_at', and 'updated_at', representing the moderation action's type, current status, creation timestamp, and last update timestamp respectively. Selecting appropriate sort fields allows users to arrange results for better usability and data analysis.

oneOf.description: The direction of the sort operation. 'asc' indicates ascending order (e.g., oldest items first), while 'desc' indicates descending order (e.g., newest items first). The server validates and enforces these two values to ensure predictable sorting behavior.

The direction of the sort operation. 'asc' indicates ascending order (e.g., oldest items first), while 'desc' indicates descending order (e.g., newest items first). The server validates and enforces these two values to ensure predictable sorting behavior.

sort_order.description: The direction of the sort operation. 'asc' indicates ascending order (e.g., oldest items first), while 'desc' indicates descending order (e.g., newest items first). The server validates and enforces these two values to ensure predictable sorting behavior.

action_type.description: Filter results to only include moderation actions of a specific type. Common action types include 'approve' for approving content, 'reject' for rejecting flagged content, 'warn' for issuing warnings to users, and 'mark_as_spam' for flagging content as spam. This filter enables moderators to focus on specific action types for streamlined workflow management.

status.description: Filter results by the current status of the moderation action. Valid statuses include 'pending' for actions awaiting review, 'approved' for confirmed actions, 'rejected' for declined actions, and 'resolved' for completed actions with follow-up. These status filters provide context-specific views for effective moderation task management.

This field is not populated by users or API consumers - it is generated automatically upon image creation and stored in the database.

This field transforms the database's article_id foreign key into an object reference, eliminating the need for secondary lookups to get article metadata when listing images.

The filename adheres to system conventions for security and consistency. It may be modified to ensure uniqueness if multiple files with the same name are uploaded, but the original name is preserved for user reference.

This field is required for image management operations and is used to identify specific file resources in the storage system.

The size is enforced within reasonable limits (up to 10MB) to maintain system performance and prevent resource exhaustion. Files exceeding 10MB cannot be uploaded and produce error responses.

This field is used for validation during upload operations and is displayed to users as part of the image metadata.

url.description:
Web-accessible URL where the image can be retrieved directly. This URL is generated by the storage service and contains a secure token for access.

The URL is stored in the database to enable direct image retrieval without requiring additional authentication for viewing, though authorization is checked at the API level.

This field is required for displaying images in the client application and is formatted as a valid URI to ensure proper integration with front-end frameworks.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this image is the primary image for the article. Primary images are displayed prominently in article listings and are used as the main visual.

Only one image can be marked as primary per article, with the system automatically unsetting other primary images when a new one is set. This field follows the "one primary image per article" business rule.

The primary image is used as the default thumbnail and is critical for content visibility.

display_order.description:
Relative position at which this image should be displayed among other images of the article. Lower values appear earlier in the display order.
The field is used to determine the sequence of images in the article's gallery. Values should be unique per article, but the system allows for gaps in numbering to facilitate adding images between existing ones without renumbering.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the image was uploaded to the system. This is a system-generated timestamp reflecting the exact moment the image was recorded in the database.

The timestamp is formatted according to ISO 8601 standards and is used for sorting, filtering, and audit purposes. It cannot be modified after creation.

This field provides critical information about when the image content was added to the system, which is important for content management and moderation workflows.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.description:
Main entity type representing a discussion board article image attachment. Contains all metadata about the attached image, including its reference to the parent article, file details, and display properties.

This type is used as the response body for article image retrieval and creation operations. It includes all fields necessary to display image information in the interface without requiring additional lookup operations.

The type excludes sensitive information and system-specific fields, focusing only on display-relevant properties that are appropriate for client-side consumption.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.IApprove.description:
Response object for the moderation queue approve-all operation. This object confirms the number of articles successfully approved when bulk-processing moderation queues.

The system returns the count of articles that were successfully moved from the moderation queue to the published state in the discussion board. This count excludes previously approved or rejected articles, and represents only the articles newly processed by the operation.

This response helps moderation teams track the success of bulk operations and verify that the expected number of articles were approved. The response is used in the moderation workflow after the approve-all operation completes, providing immediate confirmation without requiring additional API calls.

approvedCount.description:
The number of articles successfully approved by the bulk operation. This represents the count of articles that were in the moderation queue and were successfully moved to a published state. This count is the exact number of articles processed successfully by the current operation, excluding those already approved or rejected before the request.

Values range from 0 to the total pending articles in the queue, with 0 indicating no new approvals occurred. This value reflects the pre-approval state of the queue before the operation began.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the moderation queue entry. Generated by the database upon creation and serves as the primary key for tracking the moderation status of submissions.

This field is required for all queue entries and enables efficient retrieval of specific moderation records. It follows the UUID format standard for global uniqueness and ensures no collisions across different database operations.

The identifier remains constant throughout the article's moderation lifecycle, from submission to final status. It should never be modified once created to maintain data integrity for auditing purposes.

oneOf.description:
Current moderation status of the article. This field indicates whether the article is waiting for review, has been approved, or has been rejected with reasons.

The status follows a closed set of values: pending (initial stage, awaiting review), approved (passed moderation, published), or rejected (did not pass moderation, requires revision).

This field is critical for moderation workflows, allowing administrators to filter articles by their current status and manage the moderation pipeline efficiently.

This field is critical for moderation workflows, allowing administrators to filter articles by their current status and manage the moderation pipeline efficiently.

This field is critical for moderation workflows, allowing administrators to filter articles by their current status and manage the moderation pipeline efficiently.

submittedAt.description:
Timestamp of when the article submission was initially received for moderation. This represents the exact moment of submission rather than approval time.

The date-time format follows ISO 8601 standards for consistency across systems. This field establishes the chronological order of submissions, which is important for prioritizing articles based on when they were submitted.

This timestamp is system-generated and cannot be modified, serving as the immutable anchor point for the article's moderation timeline.

articleSummary.description:
Summary information about the article under moderation. This contains non-sensitive, basic article details suitable for moderation dashboard displays.

Rather than the full article content, this provides essential metadata like title, author, and basic category. It's designed to give moderators a quick overview without exposing the full content they're reviewing.

This field uses the IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary type to maintain consistency with the article entity's summary structure, but does not include article content to preserve privacy during the moderation process.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of articles in the moderation queue. Designed specifically for administrative interfaces where moderators need to efficiently review and manage queued articles without accessing sensitive content.

This type contains only essential fields for moderation workflows, including status, submission time, and a non-sensitive article summary. It excludes any fields that would require detailed content access or sensitive moderation data.

The summary is optimized for fast loading and pagination in administrative dashboards, with fields selected to provide maximum information density while maintaining privacy requirements for content moderation.

expiresAt.description: Session expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format. When set to a date in the future, the session will be valid until that time. If null, the session will inherit the system's default expiration policy. This field is optional for sessions that should use default expiration.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating a member session. Allows modifying specific properties of a member's session record to maintain active sessions, update session status, or adjust expiration policies. This DTO supports partial updates, so only included fields will be modified. The session modifications are restricted to the member themselves to maintain account security and prevent unauthorized session manipulation.\n\nWhen updating a session, you should specify only the properties you need to change. This DTO works with the discussion_board_member_sessions database model which contains session details and relationships to member accounts. The endpoint path structure ensures that only sessions belonging to the specified member are modified, and modification is restricted to the member themselves.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating article images. This schema supports search by filename, MIME type, and image dimensions while providing control over pagination settings. The endpoint uses these parameters to efficiently retrieve relevant image data from the discussion_board_article_images table, which stores uploaded images with resolution metadata and file type information for the bulletin board system.

Pagination supports client-side rendering, allowing users to navigate through large collections without overwhelming responses. Filters help reduce network bandwidth by requesting only the necessary image subsets (e.g., images of specific sizes or file types), improving frontend performance.

The implementation enforces strict parameter validation to prevent invalid requests and ensure database query efficiency, aligning with the system's requirements for optimized media gallery display across different devices and screen sizes.

page.description: Pagination page number (starting at 1). Required if limit is specified, but optional when default limit is assumed. Controls which page of results to return from the database query. The value must be at least 1 to avoid invalid page number errors.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Specifies the maximum number of images to return per response. The value is recommended to be between 1 and 100 for optimal bandwidth and performance, but the system will handle any value within technical limits.

mimeTypes.description: List of MIME types to filter images by. Filters images in the result set to include only those matching the specified content types (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Can be used to limit results to specific file formats for better rendering in the frontend.

IDiscussionBoardConfig.description:
System configuration entity for the discussion board application, representing a key-value pair with optional description. This entity stores runtime configuration settings that impact application behavior. The entity's primary purpose is to provide a standardized way to manage and retrieve configuration values, enabling dynamic application adjustments without code changes.

This entity is the foundational type for reading configuration values, providing a complete view of the configuration entry including its identifier, value, and supplementary information. The configuration entries are typically managed and modified via admin interface endpoints, with each configuration entry corresponding to a specific application feature or setting.

Key fields include:
- configCode: Unique identifier for the configuration
- configValue: Actual value for runtime use
- description (optional): Explanation for administrators

configCode.description:
Unique identifier for system configuration entries, acting as a reference for the application to fetch and utilize corresponding configuration values. This key must be standardized and consistent across the application to ensure proper functionality and avoid conflicts. Keys like 'language_setting' or 'theme' are used to define specific settings that influence the system's behavior.

All configuration keys must adhere to a naming convention (alphanumeric characters and underscores only, 1-50 characters), must be globally unique across all existing configuration entries, and must match predefined system constants for validation. This ensures that the application can reliably reference settings without ambiguous interpretation or invalid configurations.

configValue.description:
Value associated with the configuration key, which determines the actual configuration parameter used by the system. Values can represent a wide range of data types, such as strings (e.g., 'en' for English), JSON objects (for complex settings), or numeric values represented as strings (e.g., '100' for max_users).

The validation of the value depends on the configuration key: simple keys require specific formats, while complex keys may need JSON validation. Values must comply with the key's expected type, ensuring consistency and correctness. For example, the 'max_users' key's value must be a non-negative integer string representing the user count limit.

description.description:
Optional field providing detailed explanation of the configuration key and its purpose for administrative reference. This description helps administrators understand the role and usage of the configuration setting without needing to refer to code documentation.

The description should contain up to 255 characters, be written in clear English, and avoid sensitive or confidential information. Good examples include 'Defines the default language for system UI' or 'Maximum number of concurrent users allowed'.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the file attachment record. Serves as the primary key for the discussion_board_article_files table and allows for efficient database querying and reference in API requests. All file-related operations such as updates, deletions, and references to this media asset will use this identifier as the key.

This identifier is generated automatically upon file upload and cannot be modified or controlled by end users. It is strictly technical in nature and does not reflect any business meaning or content information about the file itself.

oneOf.description:
The type of file being attached, indicating its format and purpose. Only specific file types are supported and validated by the system for security and compatibility reasons.

The file_type must be one of these valid formats: PDF (Portable Document Format) for documents requiring high fidelity output, DOCX (Microsoft Word Document) for editable text documents, or XLSX (Microsoft Excel Spreadsheet) for tabular data. Supporting only these three formats helps minimize security risks while ensuring maximum usability for the intended use cases.

When determining the file_type, the system validates against a whitelist of approved extensions rather than just the file extension. This prevents malicious actors from renaming malicious files to have the right extensions.
